label: needoflaxcones
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{needoflaxcones}
	When $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace=\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$, the conicalization of weighted $2$-limits is, strictly speaking, not possible. We would need to encode the universal cocylinder $\mu$ exhibiting $W\cong {\operatorname{colim}}^{W}\hspace{1.0\horspace}{\operatorname{y}}$ (given by the Yoneda lemma) in terms of a universal cocone
	$$\widetilde{\mu}\:\Delta 1 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}{\ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]}\xspace}\left({H(-)},\hspace{1\horspace}{W}\right)$$
	with $H$ some $2$-functor $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace\to \ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]}\xspace$.  And this is not possible because the components of $\mu$ are functors rather than mere functions. The idea is to admit $2$-cells inside the cocone $\widetilde{\mu}$ in order to encode the extra data. We thus consider lax natural transformations, that have general structure 2-cells inside the naturality squares. But, as we explain in \textrm{Construction}~\ref{2SetGrothconstrtoconicalize}, the right notion of relaxed 2-natural transformation to consider will be a marked version of lax natural transformations.

label: 2SetGrothconstrtoconicalize
title: Construction
body_md:
\label{2SetGrothconstrtoconicalize}
	Following \textrm{Remark}~\ref{needoflaxcones}, we search for a relaxed notion of 2-natural transformation, which is however stronger than a lax natural transformation, and for a $2$-functor $H\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace\to \ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]}\xspace$ such that any cocylinder
		$$\varphi\:W 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}{\ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]}\xspace}\left({\ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({-}\right)}},\hspace{1\horspace}{U}\right)$$
		with $U\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$ can be encoded in terms of a relaxed $2$-natural transformation
		$$\widetilde{\varphi}\:\Delta 1  
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{\operatorname{relaxed}}{} {\ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]}\xspace}\left({H(-)},\hspace{1\horspace}{U}\right)\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}\to\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace.$$
		
		In order to deduce that every weighted $2$-limit can be analogously conicalized via the lemma of continuity of a limit in its weight, we need $H$ of the form
		$${\left(\ensuremath{{\scalebox{1.2}{$\int$}}\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.15ex} W}\right)}\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} 
	\ext@arrow 0099\arrowfill@\relbar\relbar\longrightarrow{}{{\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(W\right)}\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}} \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} 
	\ext@arrow 0099\arrowfill@\relbar\relbar\longrightarrow{}{\operatorname{y}} \ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]}\xspace.$$
		Up to now, $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ and $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(A\right)$ are just symbols, but will be found to be the {\itshape $2$-category of elements}, as defined explicitly by Street in~\cite{street_limitsindexedbycatvalued}. The explicit formulas that we find for building $\widetilde{\varphi}$ from $\varphi$ are stricter analogues of the ones of Descotte, Dubuc and Szyld's~\cite{descottedubucszyld_sigmalimandflatpseudofun} (where they essentially conicalize bilimits). 
	
		For every $A\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and $X\in W(A)$, we have a morphism $\varphi_A(X)\:\ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({A}\right)}\to U$, and we want to form the cocone $\widetilde{\varphi}$ exactly with these morphisms. So we take the objects of $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ to be all pairs $(A,X)$ with $A\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and $X\in W(A)$, and define $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(W\right)(A,X)\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} A$. We then set $\widetilde{\varphi}_{(A,X)}\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} \varphi_A(X)$.
		
		But $\widetilde{\varphi}$ also needs to encode the assignment of every $\varphi_A$ on morphisms $\alpha\:X\to X'$ in $W(A)$. Lax naturality of $\widetilde{\varphi}$ allows to have, for every $\xi\:(A,X) \to (A',X')$ in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$, a $2$-cell
		\begin{cd}[4][6]
			1 \arrow[r,"{\widetilde{\varphi}_{(A,X)}}"] \arrow[d,equal]\& {\ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]}\xspace}\left({\ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({A}\right)}},\hspace{1\horspace}{U}\right)\arrow[d,"{-\circ \ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({\hspace{1.0\horspace}\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(W\right)\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}(\xi)}\right)}}"]\arrow[dl,Rightarrow,"{\widetilde{\varphi}_\xi}"'{pos=0.43}, shorten <= 2.8ex, shorten >= 4.9ex]\\
			1 \arrow[r,"{\widetilde{\varphi}_{(A',X')}}"'] \& {\ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]}\xspace}\left({\ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({A'}\right)}},\hspace{1\horspace}{U}\right)
		\end{cd} 
		For every $A\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and $\alpha\:X\to X'$ in $W(A)$, we need a morphism $(A,X)\to (A,X')$ in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ whose image with respect to $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(W\right)$ is $\operatorname{id}_{A}$. Wishing to write the action of $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(W\right)$ as a projection on the first component, we call such morphism $(A,X)\to (A,X')$ as $(\operatorname{id}_{A},\alpha)$. We set $\widetilde{\varphi}_{(\operatorname{id}_{A},\alpha)}\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} \varphi_A(\alpha)$.
		
		We now encode the $2$-naturality of $\varphi$ into the relaxed naturality of $\widetilde{\varphi}$. For every $f\:A\to A'$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and $X\in W(A)$, the naturality of $\varphi$ expresses the equality
		$$\varphi_{A'}(W(f)(X))=\varphi_A(X)\circ \ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({f}\right)}.$$
		So, for every $f\:A\to A'$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and $X\in W(A)$, we need a morphism
		$$\underline{f}^X\:(A,X)\to (A',W(f)(X))$$
		in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ such that $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(W\right)\left(\underline{f}^X\right)=f$ and $\widetilde{\varphi}_{\underline{f}^X}=\operatorname{id}_{}$.
		
		It is natural to take $\underline{\operatorname{id}_{A}}^X=(\operatorname{id}_{A},\operatorname{id}_{X})$ for every $A\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and $X\in W(A)$ and ask any of such equal morphisms to be the identity on $(A,X)$. We then need to close the union of the two kinds of morphisms $(\operatorname{id}_{A},\alpha)$ and $\underline{f}^X$ under composition. For this, we notice that, given $f\:A\to A'$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and $\alpha\:X\to X'$ in $W(A)$, the two morphisms $\underline{f}^{X'}\circ (\operatorname{id}_{A},\alpha)$ and $(\operatorname{id}_{A'},W(f)(\alpha))\circ \underline{f}^X$ in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ will have the same associated structure $2$-cell of $\widetilde{\varphi}$, by lax naturality of $\widetilde{\varphi}$. We then take such two morphisms in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ to be equal, so that we will be able to recover the naturality of $\varphi$ (on morphisms) starting from $\widetilde{\varphi}$. At this point, every finite composition of morphisms in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ can be reduced to a composite\vspace{-1\verspace}\xspace
		$$(A,X)\xrightarrow[]{\underline{f}^X} (A',W(f)(X)) \xrightarrow[]{(\operatorname{id}_{A'},\alpha)} (A',X')$$
		for some $f\:A\to A'$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and $\alpha\:W(f)(X)\to X'$ in $W(A')$. We define the morphisms in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ to be all the formal composites $(\operatorname{id}_{A'},\alpha)\circ \underline{f}^X$, that we call $(f,\alpha)$. And we see that $\underline{f}^X=(f,\operatorname{id}_{W(f)(X)})$. Functoriality forces $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(W\right)(f,\alpha)=f$, and lax naturality forces
		$$\widetilde{\varphi}_{(f,\alpha)}=\widetilde{\varphi}_{(\operatorname{id}_{A'},\alpha)\circ (f,\operatorname{id}_{})}=\varphi_{A'}(\alpha)\circ \operatorname{id}_{}=\varphi_{A'}(\alpha).$$
		
		We now want to encode the $2$-dimensional part of the $2$-naturality of $\varphi$ into the $2$-dimensional part of the relaxed naturality of $\widetilde{\varphi}$. Lax naturality of $\widetilde{\varphi}$ allows to have, for every $2$-cell $\Xi\:(f,\alpha) 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}(g,\beta)\:(A,X)\to (A',X')$ in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$,
		\begin{eqD}{twodimlaxphitilde}
			\scalebox{0.9}{\begin{cd}*[6.5][7]
				1 \arrow[r,"{\widetilde{\varphi}_{(A,X)}}"] \arrow[d,equal]\& {\ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]}\xspace}\left({\ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({A}\right)}},\hspace{1\horspace}{U}\right)\arrow[d,"{-\circ \ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({f}\right)}}"]\arrow[dl,Rightarrow,"{\widetilde{\varphi}_{(f,\alpha)}}"{pos=0.445}, shorten <= 2.8ex, shorten >= 4.9ex]\\
				1 \arrow[r,"{\widetilde{\varphi}_{(A',X')}}"'] \& {\ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]}\xspace}\left({\ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({A'}\right)}},\hspace{1\horspace}{U}\right)
			\end{cd} = \quad
			\begin{cd}*[6.5][7]
				1 \arrow[r,"{\widetilde{\varphi}_{(A,X)}}"] \arrow[d,equal]\& 	{\ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]}\xspace}\left({\ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({A}\right)}},\hspace{1\horspace}{U}\right)\arrow[d,bend right,shift right=0ex,"{-\circ \ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({g}\right)}}"'{name=B}]\arrow[d,bend left,shift left = 2ex,"{-\circ \ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({f}\right)}}"{name=A}]\arrow[dl,Rightarrow,shift right=1ex,"{\widetilde{\varphi}_{(g,\beta)}}"{pos=0.55}, shorten <= 4.65ex, shorten >= 3.2ex]\\
				1 \arrow[r,"{\widetilde{\varphi}_{(A',X')}}"'] \& {\ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]}\xspace}\left({\ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({A'}\right)}},\hspace{1\horspace}{U}\right)
				\arrow[Rightarrow,from=A,to=B,"{-\ast \ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({\hspace{1.0\horspace}\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(W\right)\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}(\Xi)}\right)}}"'{inner sep=1ex},shorten <=1.55ex, shorten >=1.5ex]
			\end{cd}}
		\end{eqD}
		The $2$-naturality of $\varphi$ expresses the following equality, for every $2$-cell $\delta\:f 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}g\:A\to A'$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and for every $X\in W(A)$:
		$$\varphi_{A'}(W(\delta)_X)=\varphi_A(X)\hspace{1.0\horspace}\ensuremath{\operatorname{y}\hspace{-0.2ex}\left({\delta}\right)}\:\varphi_{A'}(W(f)(X)) 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}\varphi_{A'}(W(g)(X)).$$
		So, for every $2$-cell $\delta\:f 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}g\:A\to A'$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and every $X\in W(A)$, we need a $2$-cell in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$, that we call $\underline{\delta}^X$ or just $\delta$, such that
		$$\underline{\delta}^X\:(f,W(\delta)_X) 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}(g,\operatorname{id}_{})\:(A,X)\to (A',W(g)(X))$$
		and $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(W\right)(\underline{\delta}^X)=\delta$. These $2$-cells are closed under both vertical and horizontal composition, inherited from $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$, but we have to close them under whiskering with morphisms $(\operatorname{id}_{A},\alpha)$. Notice that for every $\delta\:f 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}g\:A\to A' $ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and every $\alpha\:X\to X'$ in $W(A)$, we have that the axiom of equation~$($\ref{twodimlaxphitilde}$)$ of $\widetilde{\varphi}$ on the two whiskerings $\underline{\delta}^{X'}\hspace{1.0\horspace}(\operatorname{id}_{A},\alpha)$ and $(\operatorname{id}_{A'},W(g)(\alpha))\hspace{1.0\horspace} \underline{\delta}^{X}$ in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ is exactly the same. So we ask such two whiskerings in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ to be equal. At this point, every horizontal composition of $2$-cells in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ can be reduced to a whiskering of the form $(\operatorname{id}_{},\beta)\hspace{1.0\horspace} \underline{\delta}^X$ for some $2$-cell $\delta\:f 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}g\:A\to A'$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$, $X\in W(A)$ and $\beta\:W(g)(X)\to X'$ in $W(A')$. We define the $2$-cells in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ to be precisely such formal whiskerings. Equivalently, a $2$-cell $(f,\alpha) 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}(g,\beta)\:(A,X)\to (A',X')$ in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ is a $2$-cell $\delta\:f 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}g$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ such that
		$$\alpha=\beta\circ W(\delta)_X.$$
		For this, we will call such $2$-cell just $\delta\:(f,\alpha) 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}(g,\beta)$. Compositions are inherited from $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$. Then $2$-functoriality forces $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(W\right)(\delta)=\delta$.
		
		It is straightforward to show that $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ is a $2$-category and that $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(W\right)\:\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ is a $2$-functor. Notice that we have also described the right notion of relaxed $2$-natural transformation that $\widetilde{\varphi}$ needs to satisfy to encode the $2$-naturality of $\varphi$. It is a form of marked lax natural transformation, i.e.\ a lax natural transformation such that certain structure $2$-cells are asked to be identities (\textrm{Definition}~\ref{deflaxnormal}).

body_md:
\label{motivationlaxnormal}
	Cartesian-marked lax natural transformations are a particular case of a more general notion of marked lax natural transformation introduced by Gray in~\cite{gray_formalcattheory}. They are a stricter analogue of Descotte, Dubuc and Szyld's~\cite{descottedubucszyld_sigmalimandflatpseudofun} sigma limits. ``Cartesian" refers to the fact that the marking is precisely given by the chosen cartesian liftings of the 2-category of elements $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(W\right)\:\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$. Street showed in~\cite{street_limitsindexedbycatvalued} that this less general notion is totally sufficient to build all the general limits considered by Gray.

label: laxnormalconicallimits
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{laxnormalconicallimits}
		Let $W\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$ be a $2$-functor with $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ small, and let $F\:\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W} \to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ be a $2$-functor. Notice that $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ is small, since $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ is small. The {\itshape cartesian-marked lax conical limit of $F$}, denoted as $\operatorname{lax^{cart}}\mbox{-}\hspace{1.5\horspace}{\lim}^{\Delta 1}\hspace{1.0\horspace}{F}$, is (if it exists) an object $L\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ together with an isomorphism of categories
		$${\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}\left({U},\hspace{1\horspace}{L}\right)\cong {\ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{{\scalebox{1.2}{$\int$}}\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.15ex} W},\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]_{\operatorname{lax^{cart}}}}\xspace}\left({\Delta 1},\hspace{1\horspace}{{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}\left({U},\hspace{1\horspace}{F(-)}\right)}\right)$$
		$2$-natural in $U\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}$,\vspace{1.0\verspace}\xspace where $\ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W},\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]_{\operatorname{lax^{cart}}}}\xspace$ is the $2$-category of $2$-functors, cartesian-marked lax natural transformations and modifications from $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$ to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace.
		
		\noindent When $\operatorname{lax^{cart}}\mbox{-}\hspace{1.5\horspace}{\lim}^{\Delta 1}\hspace{1.0\horspace}{F}$ exists, the identity on $L$ provides a cartesian-marked lax natural transformation $\lambda\:\Delta 1  
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{\operatorname{lax^{cart}}}{}{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}\left({L},\hspace{1\horspace}{F(-)}\right)$ called the {\itshape universal cartesian-marked lax cone}.
				
		Let $W\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\to\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$ be a $2$-functor with $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ small, and let $F\:{\left(\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}\right)}\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ be a $2$-functor. The {\itshape cartesian-marked lax conical colimit of $F$}, denoted as $\operatorname{lax^{cart}}\mbox{-}\hspace{1.5\horspace}{\operatorname{colim}}^{\Delta 1}\hspace{1.0\horspace}{F}$, is (if it exists) an object $C\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ together with a natural isomorphism of categories
		$${\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}\left({C},\hspace{1\horspace}{U}\right)\cong {\ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{{\scalebox{1.2}{$\int$}}\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.15ex} W},\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]_{\operatorname{lax^{cart}}}}\xspace}\left({\Delta 1},\hspace{1\horspace}{{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}\left({F(-)},\hspace{1\horspace}{U}\right)}\right)$$

title: Remark
body_md: We now show a new, more elementary proof of the fact that cartesian-marked lax conical limits are particular weighted $2$-limits. Street states the analogous result in~\cite{street_limitsindexedbycatvalued} for all the general $2$-limits introduced by Gray in~\cite{gray_formalcattheory}, with a complex proof that gives the weight as the coidentifier of a certain $2$-cell with horizontal codomain the weight of lax conical limits. We present an original explicit weight for cartesian-marked lax conical limits that is actually simpler than the one for lax conical limits. Indeed the latter involves quotients of lax $2$-dimensional slices (see Street's~\cite{street_limitsindexedbycatvalued}), while the former only needs ordinary $1$-dimensional slices. The reason is that the laxness of cartesian-marked lax natural transformations is concentrated in the vertical part of $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} W}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Given $\varphi\:\Delta 1  
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{\operatorname{lax^{cart}}}{}N$ a cartesian-marked lax natural transformation, we convert it into a $2$-natural transformation $[\varphi]\:\operatorname{W}^{\operatorname{lax^{cart}}} 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{} N$ setting, for every $(B,X')\in \ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} Z}$, 
		$$[\varphi]_{(B,X')}(\operatorname{id}_{X'})\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} \varphi_{(B,X')}$$
		$$[\varphi]_{(B,X')}\left(\begin{cd}*[1][0.5]
			X\arrow[rd,"{\alpha}"']\arrow[rr,"{\alpha}"] \&\& X'\arrow[ld,equal] \\
			\& X'
		\end{cd}\right)\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} \varphi_{(\operatorname{id}_{B},\alpha)}.$$
		$[\varphi]$ extends in a unique way to a $2$-natural transformation.

\label{redlaxnormalconical}
		Every weighted $2$-limit can be reduced to a cartesian-marked lax conical one. More precisely, given $2$-functors $F\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ and $W\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\to\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$ with $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ small,

		either side existing if the other does, where $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(W\right)$ is the $2$-category of elements of $W$.

body_md:
\label{defoplaxnormalconical}
		Consider 2-functors $W\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$ and $F\:\ensuremath{\int \hspace{-0.35ex} W}\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ with $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ small. title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remarchetypalthreedimclassifprocchanged}
		 To reach the right notion of pointwise Kan extension in $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$, it will be helpful to inscribe $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$ in an original idea of $2$-$\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace$-enrichment. Consider the following chain:
		$$\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Set}}\xspace\quad\leadsto\quad \ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace \quad\leadsto\quad 2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$$
		Such a chain is motivated by Weber's~\cite{weber_yonfromtwotop}, that explains how the 2-dimensional classifier of $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$, which is the archetypal elementary 2-topos, is given by the category of elements. Analogously, we can conceive the subobject classifier of $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Set}}\xspace$, which is the archetypal elementary topos, as the 0-category of elements. We will say in \textrm{Remark}~\ref{remapplelementarythreetopos} that we can think of $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$, which hosts the 2-category of elements, as the archetypal 3-dimensional elementary topos. We believe that the sequence above is best captured by what we call a {\itshape $2$-$\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace$-enrichment} with $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace=\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Set}}\xspace$:
		$$\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace\quad\leadsto\quad \ensuremath{{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace}\xspace \quad\leadsto\quad \ensuremath{2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace}$$
		Enriching over $\ensuremath{{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace}\xspace$, we should take into account the fact that $\ensuremath{{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace}\xspace$ is a monoidal $2$-category, and then take a {\itshape weak enrichment} rather than an ordinary one.

		The concept of {\itshape weak enrichment} is explored in Garner and Shulman's~\cite{garnershulman_enrichedcatasafreecocompl}, but the equivalent formulation presented below does not seem to appear in the literature.

label: consweakenrichment
title: Construction
body_md:
\label{consweakenrichment}
		Recall that if $(\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace,\otimes,I)$ is a monoidal category with coproducts such that $-\otimes -$ preserves coproducts in each variable, we can define a $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace$-enriched category as pair $(S,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace)$ with $S$ a set (of objects) and $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ a monoid in the monoidal category $\ensuremath{\left[S\times S,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace\right]}\xspace$ of square $S$-indexed matrices with entries in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace$, with the tensor product given by matrix multiplication. $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace$-enriched functors can be defined on this line as well.

		Let $(\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace,\otimes,I,\alpha,\lambda,\rho)$ be a monoidal $2$-category, i.e.\ a $2$-category $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace$ that is monoidal in the $1$-dimensional sense but such that the tensor product is a $2$-functor $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace\times \ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace$. And assume that $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace$ has coproducts and that $-\otimes -$ preserves them in each variable. Then, for every set $S$, the $2$-category $\ensuremath{\left[S\times S,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace\right]}\xspace$ is $2$-monoidal as well, with tensor product given by matrix multiplication.
		
		We define a {\itshape $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace$-weakly enriched category} as a pair $(S,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace)$ with $S$ a set (of objects) and $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ a pseudomonoid in the monoidal $2$-category $\ensuremath{\left[S\times S,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace\right]}\xspace$ of square $S$-indexed matrices with entries in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace$. Notice that a strict $2$-monoid in $\ensuremath{\left[S\times S,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace\right]}\xspace$ is a ${\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace}_{\hspace{3\horspace}0}$-enriched category with object set $S$.

		Given two $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace$-weakly enriched categories $(S,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace)$ and $(T,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace)$, we define a {\itshape $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace$-weakly enriched functor $(S,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace)\to (T,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace)$} as a pair $(F,\overline{F})$ with $F\:S\to T$ a function and $\overline{F}\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\to F^{\ast}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace$ a lax morphism between lax monoids in $\ensuremath{\left[S\times S,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace\right]}\xspace$, where 
		$$F^{\ast} \ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace =\left(S\times S\xrightarrow[]{F\times F} T\times T \xrightarrow[]{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{V}}\xspace\right).$$

		Given now $(F,\overline{F}), (G,\overline{G})\:(S,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace)\to (T,\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace)$ two $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace$-weakly enriched functors, we define a {\itshape $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace$-weakly enriched natural transformation $\varphi\:(F,\overline{F}) 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{\operatorname{lax}}{}(G,\overline{G})$} as a collection of $1$-cells
		$$\varphi_A\:I\to {\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace}\left({F(A)},\hspace{1\horspace}{G(A)}\right)$$
		in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace$ for every $A\in S$ and $2$-cells
		\begin{cd}[-0.35][3.8]
			\& \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace(A,B) \otimes I \arrow[r, "G\otimes \varphi_{A}",""'{name=A}] \&[1.9ex] \ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace(GA,GB) \otimes \ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace(FA,GA) \arrow[rd, "\operatorname{comp}"{inner sep=0.3ex}] \\
			\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace(A,B) \arrow[rd, "\lambda_{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace(A,B)}^{-1}"'{inner sep=0.3ex, pos=0.7}] \arrow[ru, "\rho_{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace(A,B)}^{-1}"{pos=0.7}] \&\&\&[-3ex] \ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace(FA,GB) \\
			\& I \otimes \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace(A,B) \arrow[r, "\varphi_{B}\otimes F"',""{name=B}] \& \ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace(FB,GB) \otimes \ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace(FA,FB) \arrow[ru, "\operatorname{comp}"'{pos=0.45}]
			\arrow[Rightarrow,from=A,to=B,shift left=2.85ex,"{\hspace{1\horspace}\varphi_{A,B}}",shorten <=1.5ex,shorten >=1.5ex]
		\end{cd}
		in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace$ for every pair $(A,B)\in S\times S$ that satisfy appropriate axioms, see Garner and Shulman's~\cite{garnershulman_enrichedcatasafreecocompl}. A notion of $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{K}}\xspace$-weakly-enriched modification can be given as well.

label: remaimatpointwise
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remaimatpointwise}
		We aim at a notion of {\itshape pointwise Kan extension in $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$} that allows us to prove (in \textrm{Theorem}~\ref{teorpointkanextforgroth}) a $2$-dimensional version of the pointwise Kan extension result that we have for the category of elements. For this we need a notion of (co)limit in the setting of $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$. There surely is a natural notion of ``external limit" in this context, i.e.\ a limit in the whole $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$, which is that of limit enriched over the $1$-category of $2$-categories and lax functors. Indeed $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$ is enriched over such $1$-category. For $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ a $2$-category, this recovers e.g.\ the natural isomorphism
		$${2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}}\left({\ensuremath{\mathpzc{U}}\xspace},\hspace{1\horspace}{{\operatorname{Id}_{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}}\mkern-1mu\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}\mkern-1mu{\operatorname{Id}_{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}}}\right)\cong {2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}}\left({\2},\hspace{1\horspace}{{2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}}\left({\ensuremath{\mathpzc{U}}\xspace},\hspace{1\horspace}{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}\right)}\right)$$
		presented by Lambert in~\cite{lambert_discretetwofib} as the universal property of the lax comma object ${\operatorname{Id}_{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}}\mkern-1mu\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}\mkern-1mu{\operatorname{Id}_{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}}$ (see \textrm{Definition}~\ref{completeunivproplaxcomma}) being the power of $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ by $\2$ in $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$.
		
		But we are more interested in an ``internal" notion of colimit, i.e.\ a notion of colimit in a $2$-$\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Set}}\xspace$-enriched category (after \textrm{Example}~\ref{exampletwosetenrichment}). This should include the notion of colimit in a $2$-category, but be able to express the laxness as well. After Section~\ref{sectionlaxnormallimits}, we use (now non-necessarily conical) cartesian-marked oplax colimits as colimits in a $2$-$\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Set}}\xspace$-category (see \textrm{Definition}~\ref{defoplaxnormaltwocolimit}). Notice that the marking is a piece of structure. These colimits are a particular case of the sigma-omega-limits (or sigma-s-limits) considered by Szyld in~\cite{szyld_limlifttheortwodimmonad} and~\cite{szyld_liftingpielimitswithstrictproj}; they are a stricter version of Descotte, Dubuc and Szyld's~\cite{descottedubucszyld_sigmalimandflatpseudofun} weighted sigma limits. By Proposition~3.18 of Szyld's~\cite{szyld_limlifttheortwodimmonad}, these colimits can all be reduced to (still marked) conical ones. However, expressing the diagram, the weight and the marking as different pieces of structure makes it easier for us to define {\itshape pointwise Kan extensions in $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$}.

\label{defoplaxnormaltwocolimit}
		Let $M\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$ (the marking), $F\:\ensuremath{\int \hspace{-0.35ex} M}\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ (the diagram) and $W\:{\left(\ensuremath{\int \hspace{-0.35ex} M}\right)}\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$ (the weight) be $2$-functors with $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ small. The {\itshape cartesian oplax colimit of $F$ marked by $M$ and weighted by $W$}, denoted as $\operatorname{oplax}_{M}^{\operatorname{cart}}\mbox{-}\hspace{1.5\horspace}{\operatorname{colim}}^{W}\hspace{1.0\horspace}{F}$, is (if it exists) an object $C\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ together with an isomorphism of categories

		$2$-natural in $U\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$. When $\operatorname{oplax}_{M}^{\operatorname{cart}}\mbox{-}\hspace{1.5\horspace}{\operatorname{colim}}^{W}\hspace{1.0\horspace}{F}$ exists, the identity on $C$ provides a cartesian-marked oplax natural transformation $\mu\:W  
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{\operatorname{oplax^{cart}}}{}{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}\left({F(-)},\hspace{1\horspace}{C}\right)$ called the {\itshape universal cartesian-marked oplax cocylinder}.
		
		We will also need to consider the case in which the domain of $F$ is expressed as $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} M}$ for some $2$-functor $M\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$, and $W\:{\left(\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} M}\right)}\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$. The {\itshape cartesian oplax colimit of $F$ opmarked by $M$ and weighted by $W$}, denoted as ${\operatorname{oplax}_{\operatorname{op}\mbox{-}{M}}^{\operatorname{cart}}}\mbox{-}\hspace{1.5\horspace}{\operatorname{colim}}^{W}\hspace{1.0\horspace}{F}$, is (if it exists) an object $C\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ together with a $2$-natural isomorphism of categories

title: Remark
body_md: We now propose an original notion of pointwise left Kan extension in $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$ along a discrete $2$-opfibration, using our definition of colimit in such setting (\textrm{Definition}~\ref{defoplaxnormaltwocolimit}). Our idea is to keep the corresponding diagram and weight considered in the (ordinarily) enriched setting (see Dubuc's~\cite{dubuc_kanextensionsinenrichedcat} or Kelly's~\cite{kelly_basicconceptsofenriched} for the classical definition), but adding the marking that we naturally have when we extend along a discrete $2$-opfibration. In \textrm{Theorem}~\ref{teorpointkanextforgroth}, this notion will allow us to prove a $2$-dimensional version of the fact that the comma object that captures the category of elements exhibits a pointwise Kan extension.

label: defpointkanextensionlaxthreecat
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{defpointkanextensionlaxthreecat}
		Consider a diagram
		\begin{cd}[5][4]
			\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace \arrow[rr,"{F}"]\arrow[d,"{K}"']\&\arrow[dl,Rightarrow,shift right=0.75ex,"{\lambda}"{pos=0.355, inner sep= 0.35ex},shorten <=1.45ex,shorten >= 3ex]\& \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace \\
			\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\arrow[rru,"L"']
		\end{cd}
		in $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$ with $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace$ small and $K$ a discrete $2$-opfibration with small fibres. Then by \textrm{Theorem}~\ref{essentialimagegivenbytwosetopf}, $K$ is isomorphic in the slice ${\raisebox{.1em}{$2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$}\mkern-1mu\left/\raisebox{-.25em}{$\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$}\right.}$ to $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(M\right)$ for some $2$-functor $M\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$. We can assume $K$ is in the form $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(M\right)$, up to whiskering the diagram with the isomorphism in the slice. Assume further that $\lambda$ is a cartesian-marked lax natural transformation with respect to $M$.
		
		We say that $\lambda$ exhibits $L$ as the {\itshape pointwise left Kan extension of $F$ along $K$}, written $L=\operatorname{Lan}_{\hspace{0.2ex}K}{F}$, if for every $A\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$
		$$L(A)\cong {\operatorname{oplax}_{\operatorname{op}\mbox{-}{M}}^{\operatorname{cart}}}\mbox{-}\hspace{1.5\horspace}{\operatorname{colim}}^{{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({K(-)},\hspace{1\horspace}{A}\right)}\hspace{1.0\horspace}{F}$$
		with universal cartesian-marked oplax cocylinder
		\begin{equation}\label{eqpointkanextensiontwocatlax}
			{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({K(-)},\hspace{1\horspace}{A}\right) 
	\ext@arrow 0099\arrowfill@\Relbar\Relbar\Longrightarrow{}{L}{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}\left({(L\circ K)(-)},\hspace{1\horspace}{L(A)}\right) 
	\ext@arrow 0099\arrowfill@\Relbar\Relbar\Longrightarrow{\operatorname{oplax^{cart}}}{{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}\left({\lambda_{-}},\hspace{1\horspace}{\operatorname{id}_{}}\right)}{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}\left({F(-)},\hspace{1\horspace}{L(A)}\right);
		\end{equation}
		or equivalently if for every $A\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and every $C\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ the functor  
		$${\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}\left({L(A)},\hspace{1\horspace}{C}\right) 
	\ext@arrow 0099\arrowfill@\relbar\relbar\longrightarrow{}{}{\ensuremath{\left[\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}},\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace\right]_{\operatorname{oplax^{cart}}}}\xspace}\left({{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({K(-)},\hspace{1\horspace}{A}\right)},\hspace{1\horspace}{{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace}\left({F(-)},\hspace{1\horspace}{C}\right)}\right)$$
		given by the cartesian-marked oplax natural transformation of equation~$($\ref{eqpointkanextensiontwocatlax}$)$ is an isomorphism of categories (notice that the $2$-naturality in $C$ and $A$ is granted, where the latter is using that $L$ is a $2$-functor).

title: Remark
body_md:
The rest of this section is dedicated to the proof that every pointwise left Kan extension in $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$ along a discrete $2$-opfibration (as defined in \textrm{Definition}~\ref{defpointkanextensionlaxthreecat}) is a weak left Kan extension in $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$ as well.
		
		For this, we need a generalization of the parametrized Yoneda lemma which is cartesian-marked oplax and lax together (\textrm{Theorem}~\ref{parametrizedyonedaoplaxnlax}). Such result does not seem to appear in the literature. While a fully lax parametrized Yoneda lemma is not possible, since it is the strict naturality that classically allow to expand the datum on the identity to a complete natural transformation, our version shows the minimal strictness needed to do so.
		
		Interestingly, in the fully strict $2$-natural case such expansion depends on the naturality of what will be our parameter $A$. Instead, we will need to expand via the slight strictness of the cartesian-marked oplax naturality in $B$, and this is harder to achieve.

body_md:
\label{parametrizedyonedaoplaxnlax}
		Let $K\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ be a $($\hspace{-1.9\horspace}{split}\hspace{0.6\horspace}$)$ discrete $2$-opfibration $($\hspace{-1.9\horspace}{with small fibres}\hspace{0.6\horspace}$)$ and $F\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}\times \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$ be a $2$-functor. There is a bijection between
		$$\alpha_{B,A}\:{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({K(B)},\hspace{1\horspace}{A}\right)\to F(B,A)$$
		$\operatorname{oplax^{cart}}\mbox{-}\operatorname{lax}$ natural in $(B,A)\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}\times \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and
		$$\eta_B\:1\to F(B,K(B))$$
		extraordinary lax natural in $B\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace$ $($\hspace{-1.9\horspace}{see Hirata's~\cite{hirata_notesonlaxends} for a definition of extraordinary lax natural transformations and modifications between them}\hspace{0.6\horspace}$)$.
		
		Moreover this bijection extends to an isomorphism of categories, considering as morphisms of the two categories respectively the modifications between $\operatorname{oplax^{cart}}\mbox{-}\operatorname{lax}$ natural transformations and the modifications between extraordinary lax natural transformations.

title: Proof
body_md:
By \textrm{Theorem}~\ref{essentialimagegivenbytwosetopf}, we can assume that $K$ is in the form $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(M\right)\:\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} M}\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ for a $2$-functor $M\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace \to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace$. Given
		$$\alpha_{(B,Y),A}\:{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({K(B,Y)},\hspace{1\horspace}{A}\right)\to F((B,Y),A)$$
		$\operatorname{oplax^{cart}}\mbox{-}\operatorname{lax}$ natural in $((B,Y),A)\in {\left(\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} M}\right)}\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}\times \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ (see \textrm{Definition}~\ref{defoplaxnlax}), we construct $\eta_{(B,Y)}$ as the composite
		$$1\xrightarrow[]{\operatorname{id}_{B}} {\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({B},\hspace{1\horspace}{B}\right)\xrightarrow[]{\alpha_{(B,Y),B}}F((B,Y),B)$$
		Then $\eta_{(B,Y)}$ is extraordinary lax natural in $(B,Y)\in \ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} M}$, with structure $2$-cell on $(g,\gamma)\:(B,Y)\to (B',Y')$ in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} M}$ given by the pasting
		\begin{eqD}{diagramfromalphatoeta}
			\begin{cd}*[4.5][4.5]
				1 \arrow[r,"{\operatorname{id}_{B}}"]\arrow[d,"{\operatorname{id}_{B'}}"']\& {\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({B},\hspace{1\horspace}{B}\right) \arrow[ld,equal,shorten <=4.75ex,shorten >=4.75ex]\arrow[d,"{g\circ -}"] \arrow[r,"{\alpha_{(B,Y),B}}"]\&F((B,Y),B) \arrow[dd,"{F(\operatorname{id}_{},g)}"] \arrow[ld,Rightarrow,"{\alpha_{(B,Y),g}}"{pos=0.61},shorten <=4.45ex,shorten >=2.25ex]
				\\
				{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({B'},\hspace{1\horspace}{B'}\right)\arrow[d,"{\alpha_{(B',Y'),B'}}"'] \arrow[r,"{-\circ g}"']\& {\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({B},\hspace{1\horspace}{B'}\right)\arrow[rd,"{\alpha_{(B,Y),B'}}"{inner sep =0.2ex, pos=0.44}]\arrow[ld,Rightarrow,"{\alpha_{(g,\gamma),B'}}"{pos=0.56},shorten <=3.9ex,shorten >=3.35ex]
				\\
				F((B',Y'),B') \arrow[rr,"{F((g,\gamma),\operatorname{id}_{})}"']\&\&F((B,Y),B')
			\end{cd}
		\end{eqD}
		
		Now, given $\eta_B\:1\to F((B,Y),B)$ extraordinary lax natural in $(B,Y)\in \ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} M}$, we expand it to functors
		$$\alpha_{(B,Y),A}\:{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({K(B,Y)},\hspace{1\horspace}{A}\right)\to F((B,Y),A)$$
		$\operatorname{oplax^{cart}}\mbox{-}\operatorname{lax}$ natural in $((B,Y),A)\in {\left(\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} M}\right)}\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}}\times \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ as follows, using the cartesian-marked oplax naturality in $(B,Y)$. Given $u\:B\to A$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$, considering $\underline{u}^{Y}=(u,\operatorname{id}_{})$, the structure $2$-cell $\alpha_{(u,\operatorname{id}_{}),A}=\operatorname{id}_{}$ will give us a commutative square
		 
	                                                               
	\def\foosq##1##2##3##4##5##6##7##8{ 
		\IfBooleanTF{#1}{\begin{cd}*}{\begin{cd}}[#3][#4]
				{##1}\ifx#2p{\arrow[rd,phantom,"\scalebox{1.6}{\color{black}$\lrcorner$}",very near start]}\fi\arrow[r,"{##5}"]\ifx#9l{\arrow[d,equal,"{##6}"']}\else{\arrow[d,"{##6}"']}\fi\&{##2}\ifx#9r{\arrow[d,equal,"{##7}"]}\else{\arrow[d,"{##7}"]}\fi\ifx#2l{\arrow[ld,Rightarrow,shorten <=#6ex,shorten >=#7ex,"{#5}"{pos=#8}]}\fi\\
				{##3}\ifx#9d{\arrow[r,equal,"{##8}"']}\else{\arrow[r,"{##8}"']}\fi\ifx#2o{\arrow[ur,Rightarrow,shorten <=#6ex,shorten >=#7ex,"{#5}"{pos=#8}]}\fi\&{##4}
		\end{cd}} 
		\foosq[n][3.8][9]{{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({A},\hspace{1\horspace}{A}\right)}{F((A,M(u)(Y)),A)}{{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({B},\hspace{1\horspace}{A}\right)}{F((B,Y),A)}{\alpha_{(A,M(u)(Y)),A}}{-\circ u}{F((u,\operatorname{id}_{}),A)}{\alpha_{(B,Y),A}}
		So, in order to reach the bijection we want, we define
		$$\alpha_{(B,Y),A}(u)\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} F((u,\operatorname{id}_{}),A)\left(\eta_{(A,M(u)(Y))}\right).$$
		Given $\theta\:u 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{} v\:B\to A$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$, considering
		$$\underline{\theta}^{Y}\:(u,M(\theta)_Y) 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}(v,\operatorname{id}_{})\:(B,Y)\to (A,M(v)(Y))$$
		and using that $\alpha_{(v,\operatorname{id}_{}),A}=\operatorname{id}_{}$, we will have by the $2$-dimensional axiom of cartesian-marked oplax naturality that
		$$\alpha_{(B,Y),A}(\theta)=F(\underline{\theta}^Y,A)_{\hspace{1.0\horspace}\alpha_{(A,M(v)(Y)),A}(\operatorname{id}_{A})}\circ {\left(\alpha_{(u,M(\theta)_Y),A}\right)}_{\operatorname{id}_{A}}$$
		So we firstly define the components of the structure $2$-cells that express the cartesian-marked oplax naturality of $\alpha_{(B,Y),A}$ in $(B,Y)$ and then we will read how to define the action of $\alpha_{(B,Y),A}$ on morphisms $\theta$.
		
		Looking at the diagram of equation~$($\ref{diagramfromalphatoeta}$)$ applied to $(\operatorname{id}_{B},\gamma)\:(B,Y)\to (B,Y')$ in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} M}$, we see that, in order to have a bijection between the $\alpha$'s and the $\eta$'s, we need to define
		$${\left(\alpha_{(\operatorname{id}_{B},\gamma),B}\right)}_{\operatorname{id}_{B}}\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} \eta_{(\operatorname{id}_{B},\gamma)}.$$
		Whence, given arbitrary $(g,\gamma)\:(B,Y)\to (B',Y')$ in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} M}$ and $w\:B'\to A$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$, since 
		$$(w,\operatorname{id}_{})\circ (g,\gamma)=(\operatorname{id}_{A},M(w)(\gamma))\circ (w\circ g,\operatorname{id}_{}),$$ we need to define
		$${\left(\alpha_{(g,\gamma),A}\right)}_w\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} F((w\circ g,\operatorname{id}_{}),A)\left(\eta_{(\operatorname{id}_{A},M(w)(\gamma))}\right).$$
		And at this point we define, by the argument above,
		$$\alpha_{(B,Y),A}(\theta)\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} F(\underline{\theta}^Y,A)_{\eta_{(A,M(v)(Y))}}\circ F((u,\operatorname{id}_{}),A)\left(\eta_{(\operatorname{id}_{A},M(\theta)_Y)}\right)$$
		for every $\theta\:u 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}v\:B\to A$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$.
		
		Looking at the diagram of equation~$($\ref{diagramfromalphatoeta}$)$ applied to $(g,\operatorname{id}_{})\:(B,Y)\to (B',M(g)(Y))$ in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} M}$, we see that, in order to have the bijection we want, we need to define
		$${\left(\alpha_{(B,Y),g}\right)}_{\operatorname{id}_{B}}\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} \eta_{(g,\operatorname{id}_{})}.$$
		Whence, given an arbitrary $f\:A\to A'$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$ and $u\:K(B,Y)\to A$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$, by the compatibility axiom of $\operatorname{oplax^{cart}}\mbox{-}\operatorname{lax}$ applied to $(u,\operatorname{id}_{})\:(B,Y)\to (A,M(u)(Y))$ in $\ensuremath{\int\ensuremath{^{\operatorname{op}}} \hspace{-0.35ex} M}$ and $f\:A\to A'$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$, we need to define
		$${\left(\alpha_{(B,Y),f}\right)}_u\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} F((u,\operatorname{id}_{}),A')\left(\eta_{(f,\operatorname{id}_{})}\right).$$
		
		Now, we verify that such assignments work. To show that $\alpha_{(B,Y),A}$ is a functor, consider $u 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{\theta} v 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{\rho}w\:B\to A$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$. Then
		$$\alpha_{(B,Y),A}(\rho\circ \theta)\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} F(\underline{(\rho\circ \theta)}^Y,A)_{\eta_{(A,M(w)(Y))}}\circ F((u,\operatorname{id}_{}),A)\left(\eta_{(\operatorname{id}_{A},M(\rho\circ\theta)_Y)}\right)$$
		while $\alpha_{(B,Y),A}(\rho)\circ\alpha_{(B,Y),A}(\theta)$ is equal to
		$$\scalebox{0.935}{$F(\underline{\rho}^Y,A)_{\eta_{(A,M(w)(Y))}}\circ F((v,\operatorname{id}_{}),A)\left(\eta_{(\operatorname{id}_{A},M(\rho)_Y)}\right)\circ F(\underline{\theta}^Y,A)_{\eta_{(A,M(v)(Y))}}\circ F((u,\operatorname{id}_{}),A)\left(\eta_{(\operatorname{id}_{A},M(\theta)_Y)}\right)$}$$
		By the extraordinary naturality of $\eta$,
		$$\eta_{(\operatorname{id}_{A},M(\rho\circ \theta)_Y)}=F((\operatorname{id}_{A},M(\theta)_Y),A)\left(\eta_{(\operatorname{id}_{A},M(\rho)_Y)}\right)\circ \eta_{(\operatorname{id}_{A},M(\theta)_Y)}$$
		And by the uniqueness of the liftings of $2$-cells through $\mathcal{G}\mkern-1.4mu\left(M\right)$, we have that
		$$\underline{(\rho\circ \theta)}^Y=\underline{\rho}^Y\circ (\operatorname{id}_{A},M(\rho)_Y)\hspace{1.0\horspace} \underline{\theta}^Y.$$
		So, by $2$-functoriality of $F$, it suffices to prove that
		$$F(\underline{\theta}^Y,A)_{F((\operatorname{id}_{A},M(\rho)_Y),A)\left(\eta_{(A,M(w)_Y)}\right)}\circ F((u,M(\theta)_Y),A)\left(\eta_{(\operatorname{id}_{A},M(\rho)_Y)}\right)$$
		is equal to
		$$F((v,\operatorname{id}_{}),A)\left(\eta_{(\operatorname{id}_{A},M(\rho)_Y)}\right)\circ F(\underline{\theta}^Y,A)_{\eta_{(A,M(v)(Y))}}.$$
		And this is true by naturality of $F(\underline{\theta}^Y,A)$.
		The fact that ${\left(\alpha_{(B,Y),f}\right)}_u$ is a natural transformation is checked with techniques similar to the above ones, noticing that $\underline{(f\hspace{1.0\horspace}\theta)}^Y=(f,\operatorname{id}_{})\hspace{1.0\horspace}\underline{\theta}^Y$. Whereas showing that ${\left(\alpha_{(g,\gamma),A}\right)}_w$ is a natural transformation uses that for $(g,\gamma)\:(B,Y)\to (B',Y')$
		$$\underline{(\theta\hspace{1.0\horspace} g)}^{Y}=\underline{\theta}^{M(g)(Y)}\hspace{1.0\horspace} (g,\operatorname{id}_{})\quad \text{and}\quad \underline{\theta}^{Y'}\hspace{1.0\horspace}(\operatorname{id}_{},\gamma)=(\operatorname{id}_{},M(v)(\gamma))\hspace{1.5\horspace}\underline{\theta}^{M(g)(Y)}.$$
		At this point, it is straightforward to check that $\alpha_{(B,Y),A}$ is $\operatorname{oplax^{cart}}\mbox{-}\operatorname{lax}$ in $((B,Y),A)$. And we immediately see that we obtain a bijection between the $\alpha$'s and the $\eta$'s.
		
		We extend such bijection to an isomorphism of categories. We send a modification $$\Theta_{(B,Y),A}\:\alpha_{(B,Y),A} 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}\beta_{(B,Y),A}\:{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({K(B,Y)},\hspace{1\horspace}{A}\right)\to F((B,Y),A)$$
		between $\operatorname{oplax^{cart}}\mbox{-}\operatorname{lax}$ natural transformations in $((B,Y),A)$ to the modification
		\begin{cd}[2.5][6.5]
			1 \arrow[r,"{\operatorname{id}_{B}}"]\&[-1ex]{\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace}\left({B},\hspace{1\horspace}{B}\right)\arrow[r,bend left=24,"{\alpha_{(B,Y),B}}",""'{name=A}]\arrow[r,bend right=24,"{\beta_{(B,Y),B}}"',""{name=B}]\&F((B,Y),B)
			\arrow[Rightarrow,from=A,to=B,shift right=0.5ex,"{\Theta_{(B,Y),B}}"{description,pos=0.46},shorten <=0.15ex,shorten >=0ex]
		\end{cd}
		between extraordinary lax natural transformations. We then send a modification
		$$\Gamma_{(B,Y)}\:\eta_{(B,Y)} 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}{\eta'}_{(B,Y)}\:1\to F((B,Y),B)$$
		between extraordinary lax natural transformations to the modification $\Theta$ between $\operatorname{oplax^{cart}}\mbox{-}\operatorname{lax}$ natural transformations such that for every $u\:B\to A$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace$
		$${\left(\Theta_{(B,Y),A}\right)}_{u}\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} F((u,\operatorname{id}_{}),A)\left(\Gamma_{(A,M(u)(Y))}\right).$$
		The two assignments are clearly functorial and inverses of each other.

			\begin{eqD*}

	\ext@arrow 0099\arrowfill@\equiv\equiv 
	\DOTSB\protect\equiv\protect\joinrel\Rrightarrow{}{\Xi}\quad

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{laxcommaisobject}
		Let $F\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ and $G\:\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace\to \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace$ be $2$-functors. There is a lax natural transformation
		\begin{cd}[5.8][5.8]
			{F}\mkern-1mu\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}\mkern-1mu{G} \arrow[r,"{\partial_0}"]\arrow[d,"{\partial_1}"']\& \ensuremath{\mathpzc{A}}\xspace\arrow[d,"{F}"]\arrow[ld,Rightarrow,"{\lambda}",shorten <= 2.7ex, shorten >=2.2ex]\\
			\ensuremath{\mathpzc{B}}\xspace\arrow[r,"{G}"']\& \ensuremath{\mathpzc{C}}\xspace
		\end{cd}
		that exhibits the lax comma ${F}\mkern-1mu\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}\mkern-1mu{G}$ as the lax comma object in $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$ from $F$ to $G$. Moreover, in the condition $(ii)$ of lax comma object in $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$, if $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ $($\hspace{-1.9\horspace}{that can be lax natural}\hspace{0.6\horspace}$)$ are both strict $2$-natural $($\hspace{-1.9\horspace}{resp. pseudo-natural}\hspace{0.6\horspace}$)$ then also $\nu$ is so.

title: Proof
body_md:
Firstly, we construct $\lambda$. Given $(A,B,h)\in {F}\mkern-1mu\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}\mkern-1mu{G}$, we define the component of $\lambda$ on it to be $h$. Given a morphism $(f,g,\varphi)\:(A,B,h)\to (A',B',h')$ in ${F}\mkern-1mu\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}\mkern-1mu{G}$, we define the structure $2$-cell of $\lambda$ on it to be $\varphi$. It is then straightforward to show that $\lambda$ is a lax natural transformation.
		
		For condition $(i)$ of lax comma object in $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$, since $\lambda$ picks the third component of objects and morphisms in ${F}\mkern-1mu\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}\mkern-1mu{G}$ and the other two components are determined by the projections through $\partial_0$ and $\partial_1$, we have to define $V$ as
		$$V(M)\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} (P(M),Q(M),\gamma_M)$$
		$$V(m)\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} (P(m),Q(m),\gamma_m)$$
		for every $M\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{M}}\xspace$ and every morphism $m$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{M}}\xspace$. This is easily checked to be a $2$-functor, and it works by construction.
		
		For $(ii)$, take an arbitrary $\Xi$ as above. We see that the three requests
		$$\partial_0\hspace{1.0\horspace} \nu=\Gamma, \quad \partial_1\hspace{1.0\horspace} \nu=\Delta, \quad \lambda_{\nu}=\Xi$$
		force us to construct the component of $\nu$ on an arbitrary $M\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{M}}\xspace$ to be the morphism $(\Gamma_M,\Delta_M,\Xi_M)$ in ${F}\mkern-1mu\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}\mkern-1mu{G}$. Then the structure $2$-cell of $\nu$ on a morphism $m\:M\to M'$ in $\ensuremath{\mathpzc{M}}\xspace$, being a $2$-cell in ${F}\mkern-1mu\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}\mkern-1mu{G}$, is determined by its projections through $\partial_0$ and $\partial_1$. So we are forced to define $\nu_m$ to be the $2$-cell $(\Gamma_m,\Delta_m)$ in ${F}\mkern-1mu\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}\mkern-1mu{G}$. This is indeed a $2$-cell since $\Xi$ is a modification. It is straightforward to check that $\nu$ is a lax natural transformation, since $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ are so. And we immediately see that if both $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ are strict $2$-natural (resp. pseudo-natural) then also $\nu$ is so. The observation that $\nu$ is then the unique lax natural transformation $V 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{\operatorname{lax}}{}W$ such that the modification corresponding to the lax interchange rule in $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$ of $\nu$ and $\lambda$ coincides with $\Xi$ follows from \textrm{Remark}~\ref{needof2catlax}. 
		
		For $(iii)$, let $M\in \ensuremath{\mathpzc{M}}\xspace$. Since the component $\Theta_M$ will be a $2$-cell in ${F}\mkern-1mu\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}\mkern-1mu{G}$, it is determined by its projections through $\partial_0$ and $\partial_1$. So we need to define
		$$\Theta_M\mathrel{\mathrel{\mathop:}\mkern-1.2mu=} (\Phi_M,\Psi_M).$$
		That this is indeed a $2$-cell $\nu_M 
	\ext@arrow 0055{\Rightarrowfill@}{}{}\omega_M$ in ${F}\mkern-1mu\mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}\mkern-1mu{G}$ is guaranteed by equation~$($\ref{tridimpartcompleteunivproplaxcomma}$)$, taking components on $M$. The $\Theta_M$'s organize into a modification thanks to the fact that $\Phi$ and $\Psi$ are modifications.

title: Remark
body_md:
Notice from \textrm{Definition}~\ref{completeunivproplaxcomma} that the lax comma object in a lax $3$-category really is an upgrade of the comma object to a lax $3$-dimensional ambient. Indeed, a lax comma object in a $2$-category is precisely a comma object, since any $\Xi$ of \textrm{Definition}~\ref{completeunivproplaxcomma} is then forced to be the identity, and the tridimensional part becomes trivial.

		Interestingly, the uniqueness in the $2$-dimensional part of the universal property of the lax comma object in a lax $3$-category is obtained by considering the lax interchange rule.
		
		The universal property of \textrm{Proposition}~\ref{univproplaxcommagray} is obtained precisely by restricting ourselves to consider as $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ only strict $2$-natural transformations.

body_md: The following theorem is original, refining the result of Bird in~\cite{bird_limitsintwocatoflocpresented} that the $2$-category of elements is given by a lax comma. The actual difference between our result and Bird's one is that ours allows to consider lax natural transformations $\Gamma$ and $\Delta$ in the $2$-dimensional part of the universal property. title: Remark
body_md:
\label{remapplelementarythreetopos}
		\textrm{Theorem}~\ref{grothconstrislaxcomma} shows a potential application of this work to $3$-dimensional elementary topos theory. After \textrm{Theorem}~\ref{grothconstrislaxcomma}, we should indeed view $2\hspace{2\horspace}\mbox{-}\ensuremath{\mathpzc{Cat}}\xspace_{\hspace{-1\horspace}\operatorname{lax}}$ as the archetypal example of a would-be notion of elementary $3$-topos. Its classification process is the $2$-category of elements, generalizing Weber's idea in~\cite{weber_yonfromtwotop} that the category of elements is the archetypal $2$-dimensional classification process. Towards a definition of elementary $3$-topos, one can choose between two ways. We can either regulate the classification process with lax comma objects in a lax $3$-category (as originally defined here in \textrm{Definition}~\ref{completeunivproplaxcomma}) or take pullbacks along discrete $2$-opfibrations (that serve as replacement).
